items.followUp: State four characteristics of a suspension.

rubric.why: A colloid is a heterogeneous mixture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a colloid is heterogeneous.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles are intermediate in size between those in a true solution and a suspension.
rubric.description: Gives the particle-size range or compares particle size with solutions and suspensions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the approximate range or a correct comparison.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles remain dispersed and do not settle on standing.
rubric.description: States that colloidal particles do not settle on standing.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles scatter a beam of light, producing the Tyndall effect.
rubric.description: Identifies light scattering or the Tyndall effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either term or a clear description.

modelAnswer: A colloid is a heterogeneous mixture.
Its particles have sizes intermediate between those of a true solution and a suspension (about 1–1000 nm).
The particles do not settle on standing.
Colloidal particles scatter light; this is called the Tyndall effect.

items.followUp: Write the chemical formulae of water and carbon dioxide.

rubric.why: Ammonia has one nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms.
The molecular formula of sucrose, commonly called table sugar, is C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.

items.followUp: Define the atomic number and mass number of an atom.

rubric.why: Atomic number is determined by the number of protons in the nucleus.
rubric.description: Defines atomic number as the number of protons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The mass number counts the protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
rubric.description: Defines mass number as the total number of protons and neutrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including both kinds of nuclear particles.

modelAnswer: Atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
Mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.

items.followUp: State two postulates of Rutherford’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Classical physics predicts that revolving electrons should lose energy and fall into the nucleus, so the model could not explain atomic stability.
rubric.description: Explains that Rutherford’s model could not account for the stability of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that orbiting electrons should lose energy and collapse into the nucleus.

rubric.why: The model did not explain why atoms produce discrete line spectra.
rubric.description: Explains that Rutherford’s model could not account for atomic line spectra.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the unexplained discrete spectrum.

modelAnswer: Rutherford’s model could not explain atomic stability: revolving electrons should radiate energy and spiral into the nucleus.
It could not explain the discrete line spectra of atoms, such as the hydrogen spectrum.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a principal energy level and an orbital.

rubric.why: A shell is a principal energy level around the nucleus and may be labelled K, L, M, N, or by the principal quantum number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a shell as a principal energy level.

rubric.why: A subshell is a subdivision within a shell and is labelled s, p, d, or f.
rubric.description: Defines or identifies a subshell and its relation to a shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that subshells are subdivisions of shells.

modelAnswer: A shell is a principal energy level around the nucleus, labelled K, L, M, N or by its principal quantum number.
A subshell is a subdivision of a shell, labelled s, p, d or f.

items.followUp: State two ways in which elements are arranged in the long form periodic table.

rubric.why: The long form periodic table has 18 vertical groups.
rubric.description: States a correct feature about groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that there are 18 groups or that groups are vertical columns.

rubric.why: The long form periodic table has 7 horizontal periods.
rubric.description: States a correct feature about periods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that there are 7 periods or that periods are horizontal rows.

modelAnswer: The long form periodic table has 18 vertical groups.

rubric.why: Atomic radius is commonly defined as half the distance between the nuclei of two identical bonded atoms; it also represents the distance from the nucleus to the outermost shell in the elementary atomic model.
rubric.description: Defines atomic radius using the standard inter-nuclear distance or nucleus-to-outermost-shell description.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a correct definition; award 1 mark for an incomplete but relevant definition.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is half the distance between the nuclei of two identical bonded atoms; it represents the distance from the nucleus to the outermost shell of an atom.

rubric.why: Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom; the standard definition specifies the minimum energy for this process.
rubric.description: Defines ionization energy as the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete definition; award 1 mark if the energy and electron removal are stated but the gaseous isolated atom condition is omitted.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the minimum energy required to remove an electron from the outermost shell of an isolated gaseous atom.
